source.description:
The database rows come from: `type` selects the source adapter, the
rest of the table is that adapter's options.

stream.description:
The stream between the source side and the sinks: `type` selects the
adapter, the rest is its options. Omitted means the in-process channel
with its defaults.

prefix.description:
Literal prefix prepended to every index name flusso owns (indexes,
aliases, and the flusso_meta index), so several deployments can share
one OpenSearch cluster without colliding: `dev_` gives `dev_users`.
Include any separator yourself. `--index-prefix` / `FLUSSO_INDEX_PREFIX`
override it at run time (flag > env > file). The flusso-query consumer
must apply the same prefix. Empty (the default) means no prefix.

on_error.description:
What to do when a sink rejects a document at the item level (a mapping
conflict, a malformed value): stop the run, or skip the document and
continue. Each `[[index]]` may override it.

batch.description:
How the ingest engine groups live changes into a batch. Omitted keys
keep the engine defaults; `--batch-max-changes` / `--batch-max-delay-ms`
and their `FLUSSO_*` variables override them (flag > env > file).

concurrency.description:
How much the pipeline does at once. Never written into `flusso.lock`:
`--writes` / `FLUSSO_WRITES` and `--builds` / `FLUSSO_BUILDS` override
it, and give it to `run --locked`
(flag > env > file).

backoff.description:
How long flusso waits before trying again: a failed engine's restart,
a parked lane's probe, a re-staged lane's next staging. Never written
into `flusso.lock`: `--backoff-initial-ms` / `FLUSSO_BACKOFF_INITIAL_MS`
and `--backoff-max-ms` / `FLUSSO_BACKOFF_MAX_MS` override it, and give
it to `run --locked` (flag > env > file).

server.description:
Bind addresses for the operational HTTP surfaces. The `FLUSSO_*`
variables and CLI flags override these (flag > env > file).

sinks.description:
Named sink destinations. Each key is the sink name; `type` selects the
adapter, `backfill` is the one universal key, and the rest of the table
is the adapter's options. With no sinks, `run` uses a stdout sink.

index.description: One entry per index to build.

title: flusso Config
description: One flusso deployment: one source, one stream, its sinks, and the indexes to build.

SchemaPath.description: Path to the index schema YAML file, resolved relative to the config file's directory.

oneOf.description:
Stop the run on the first rejected document. The batch is left
unconfirmed and redelivered on restart, so a persistently-bad document
halts sync until the data is fixed or the policy is changed. The default,
because dropping data should be opt-in.

Quarantine each rejected document (surfaced via metrics/status and logs)
and continue: the rest of the batch is applied, the slot advances, and
the poison is not redelivered — it simply never lands until its source
row changes again.

FailurePolicy.description:
What the pipeline does when a sink **rejects a document at the item level** —
it accepted the batch but refused a specific document (a mapping conflict, a
malformed value). Distinct from a flush-wide failure, which always stops the
run. Set globally on the config and overridable per index (both live in the
`config` crate's `Config`/`Index`, which assemble this policy).

max_changes.description:
Commit a batch once this many changes have accumulated (default 256).
A batch is also committed the moment the live stream has nothing more
ready, so a lone change never waits for a full batch; this caps a
burst. `1` flushes per change.

max_delay_ms.description:
The longest a batch stays open after its first change while changes
keep arriving, in milliseconds (default 50). Also the window a backfill
snapshot waits for straggling requests from other sinks.

Batch.description:
How live changes are grouped into one batch, from a `flusso.toml` `[batch]`
table. Both keys are optional; an omitted key keeps the engine's default.
`--batch-max-changes` / `--batch-max-delay-ms` (and their `FLUSSO_*` env
vars) override them at run time (flag > env > file).

writes.description:
Bulk writes each sink runs at once (default 4). Two writes never hold
the same document, and live changes go before backfill pages. `1`
writes one lane item at a time. At most 64.

builds.description:
Document builds the ingest engine runs at once (default 4). A document
is never built twice at once, and each lane still gets batches in the
order they were started. Live batches go before backfill pages. `1`
builds one batch at a time. At most 32; the source holds `builds + 2`
connections (`builds + 1` building, one resolving changes).

max_built_mib.description:
MiB of built documents held before the ingest engine waits (default
512): what it built and every sink has not yet acknowledged. A
backfill holds at most half of it, so live changes always have room,
and a batch larger than the whole budget still builds, alone. Counts
heap, not JSON: a document holds 8–10× its JSON size. At least 16, at
most 1,048,576.

index_budget_share.description:
The share of `max_built_mib` one index's live documents may hold
while two or more indexes run (default 0.5): one index bursting fills
at most this much, and the others keep building beside it. Its
backfill counts with every backfill against half the budget instead.
Above 0, at most 1; with one index it does nothing. `check`, `build`
and `run` refuse a value outside (0, 1].

max_waiting_per_index.description:
Documents one index may have waiting to be built before the ingest
engine stops reading changes (default `2 × [batch] max_changes`,
512, or `max_waiting` when that is set lower): how far reading runs
ahead of the builds, per index. A stop builds what was read, so this
bounds a stop's work too. At least 1; `check`, `build` and `run`
refuse 0.

max_waiting.description:
Documents every index together may have waiting to be built, and
changes read ahead of the builds, before the ingest engine stops
reading (default `2 × builds × [batch] max_changes`, 2,048, or
`max_waiting_per_index` when that is set higher). With both set, at
least `max_waiting_per_index`; `check`, `build` and `run` refuse 0 or
less.

max_pending_documents.description:
Documents every held index together may have waiting before the
ingest engine stops reading changes for every index (default
1,000,000). With two or more indexes, an index held by the memory
budget or a full lane stops no other index's reading once it has
`max_waiting_per_index` documents waiting: its changes are kept as
documents to build, about 266 B each, up to this many over every such
index. At least 1; `check`, `build` and `run` refuse 0.

Concurrency.description:
How much the pipeline does at once, from a `flusso.toml` `[concurrency]`
table. A property of the machine that runs flusso, not of the deployment:
it is never written into `flusso.lock`, so `run --locked` takes it from
`--writes` / `FLUSSO_WRITES` and `--builds` / `FLUSSO_BUILDS` or the
defaults. Every key is optional.

initial_ms.description: The first wait, in milliseconds (default 1000). At least 1.

max_ms.description:
The longest wait, in milliseconds (default 60000, or `initial_ms`
when that is larger). At least `initial_ms`; equal to it, every wait
is the same.

Backoff.description:
How long flusso waits before trying again, from a `flusso.toml`
`[backoff]` table: a failed engine's restart (sink or ingest), a parked
lane's probe, a re-staged lane's next staging. Each wait starts at
`initial_ms` and doubles, up to `max_ms`; equal values wait a constant
interval. An unset `max_ms` is 60000 or `initial_ms`, whichever is larger,
so raising the first wait alone never needs the cap; a `max_ms` set below
`initial_ms` is refused by `check`, `build` and `run` alike. A property of the machine that runs flusso: never written into
`flusso.lock`, so `run --locked` takes it from `--backoff-initial-ms` /
`FLUSSO_BACKOFF_INITIAL_MS` and `--backoff-max-ms` / `FLUSSO_BACKOFF_MAX_MS`
or the defaults (flag > env > file). Every key is optional.

Server.description:
Bind addresses for the two operational HTTP surfaces, from a `flusso.toml`
`[server]` table. Both are optional — the binary layers `FLUSSO_*` env vars
and CLI flags on top (which win), falling back to built-in defaults when all
are absent. Each is a `host:port` socket address, parsed and validated at
config-read time by [`SocketAddr`]'s own deserializer.

type.description: The adapter that implements this port.

backfill.description:
Whether this sink is ever backfilled. `false` makes it receive live
changes only, never a snapshot: the opt-out for a stateless sink beside a
stateful one, which would otherwise be re-seeded on every restart.

SinkEntry.description:
One `[sinks.<name>]` table: the adapter's port entry plus the universal
sink keys every sink engine honors regardless of adapter.

name.description:
The index's logical name; the OpenSearch alias and the `flusso-query`
binding use it.

schema.description: Path to the index's `*.schema.yml`, relative to the config file.

enabled.description:
Whether this run builds and follows the index. A disabled index keeps
its entry but is neither seeded nor updated.

on_error.description:
Per-index override of the global [`on_error`](crate::toml::ConfigToml::on_error)
policy. Omitted inherits the global default.

sinks.description:
Per-sink options for this index only, keyed by sink name: each value
is that sink's per-index options (an OpenSearch sink takes
`index_settings`). The sink's adapter validates them; a name that is no
declared sink is an error.

IndexEntry.description: One `[[index]]` entry: an index to build from a schema file.

IndexName.description: An index name: lowercase letters, digits, and underscores, not starting with a digit, at most 63 characters.

source_postgres_Connection.description: A connection URL (literal or `{ env = "VAR" }`), or a table of connection parts.

Secret.description: A literal value, or `{ env = "VAR" }` to read it from the environment at run time.

password.description: The role's password, literal or `{ env = "VAR" }`.

source_postgres_Parts.description:
The parts table, used only to deserialize the `Parts` arm so serde's field
defaults and unknown-field rejection apply without re-deriving them by hand.

oneOf.description: Use TLS if the server offers it, without verifying anything.
Require TLS, without verifying the certificate.
Require TLS and verify the certificate against the CA bundle.
Require TLS, verify the certificate, and check the hostname.

source_postgres_SslMode.description: `sslmode` for the source connection, in libpq's terms.

connection_url.description:
How the database is reached: a URL, literal or `{ env = "VAR" }`, or a
table of parts (`host`, `port`, `user`, `password`, `database`).

manage_publication.description:
Whether flusso may create or extend the publication to cover every table
the indexes read, when the source role is privileged enough. `false`
makes flusso only report coverage gaps and never issue publication DDL.

manage_replica_identity.description:
Whether flusso may set `REPLICA IDENTITY FULL` on every table an index
reads, before the slot is created: a child table then carries its parent
link (a deleted or re-parented row rebuilds its old parent), and an
update that changes no column a document reads rebuilds nothing. Needs
ownership of the table; every update and delete then logs the whole old
row (more WAL). A `USING INDEX` identity whose index already carries
the whole primary key and every parent link is kept as it is. `false`
makes flusso only report and never issue the `ALTER`.

slot.description: The logical replication slot flusso consumes. Created on first run.

ssl_root_cert.description:
PEM file of trusted CA certificates for the `verify-*` modes. Overrides
the URL's `sslrootcert`.

ssl_cert.description:
Client certificate chain PEM for mutual TLS; pairs with `ssl_key`.
Overrides the URL's `sslcert`.

ssl_key.description:
Client private key PEM for mutual TLS; pairs with `ssl_cert`. Overrides
the URL's `sslkey`.

ssl_sni_hostname.description:
SNI hostname sent in the TLS handshake when it differs from the
connection host (IP connections, load balancers).

capacity.description:
Deprecated, and ignored: still accepted, with a warning at start.
What the lanes hold is bounded in bytes by `[concurrency]
max_built_mib`, which a sink that stops acknowledging fills, pacing
ingest; each lane keeps a fixed backstop of 1,048,576 items.

oneOf.description:
Built-in OpenSearch components only: works on any cluster with no
plugins. Accent and case folding via `asciifolding` + `lowercase`.

The `analysis-icu` plugin (`icu_tokenizer` / `icu_folding` /
`icu_normalizer`) for stronger multilingual handling. Requires the plugin
on every node, or index creation fails.

sink_opensearch_TextAnalysis.description: Which analyzer toolkit the sink wires its `flusso_*` analyzers onto.

url.description: Base URL of the cluster, literal or `{ env = "VAR" }`.

tls_verify.description:
Verify TLS certificates against the Mozilla root bundle built into
flusso, plus `ca_file`; the OS trust store is not read. Set `false` for
a local cluster with a self-signed certificate.

ca_file.description:
A PEM bundle of CA certificates trusted on top of the built-in Mozilla
roots, for a cluster behind a private CA. Read when the sink starts: a
missing file, or one with no certificate, stops the start. A relative
path is resolved against flusso's working directory.

max_bytes.description:
Maximum serialized size of one bulk request, in bytes. A write is split
so no request exceeds this, independent of `batch_size`, keeping
requests under OpenSearch's `http.max_content_length` (100 MB by
default). A single document larger than this is sent on its own.

max_retries.description:
Retries for a transient bulk failure: a whole request that failed, or
documents OpenSearch refused as busy (HTTP 429 or 503), which are resent
alone. Busy documents left after the last retry fail the write, and the
batch is redelivered. A refused TLS certificate is never retried.

pipeline.description: An ingest pipeline applied to every indexed document.

number_of_shards.description: Primary shards for each index flusso creates.

number_of_replicas.description: Replica shards for each index flusso creates.

refresh_interval.description:
The `refresh_interval` applied to each index once its backfill completes:
the steady-state visibility ceiling (`"10s"`, `"1s"`, or `"-1"` to
disable automatic refresh). Indexes are seeded with refresh off and
handed this value afterwards; a write that catches the pipeline up
forces an immediate refresh of everything written before it, so this
only bounds staleness while a backlog drains.

text_analysis.description: Which analysis toolkit the built-in `flusso_*` analyzers use.

auto_subfields.description:
Whether `text`/`keyword` fields are enriched with a good analyzer and the
`keyword` / `keyword_lowercase` / `text` subfields. A field's explicit
mapping always wins.

index_settings.description:
Extra OpenSearch index settings for every index this sink creates, e.g.
`{ "mapping.total_fields.limit" = 5000 }`. Applied when an index
generation is created. Keys, precedence, and the keys flusso owns are in
the Sink: OpenSearch reference, under Index settings.

pretty.description:
Pretty-print each envelope over several lines instead of one compact
JSON line per operation.

index_settings.description:
OpenSearch index settings for this index only, laid over the sink's
`index_settings`. Same keys and rules.

sink_opensearch_index.description:
The options an OpenSearch sink takes per index: an `[[index]]` entry's
`[index.sinks.<name>]` table, where `<name>` is the OpenSearch sink.
sink_opensearch_index.title: opensearch (per index)
